Red wine over a white carpet?
Catch a falling banknote and it's yours.
It drops faster than you can react.
In online games, you react faster than your own internet.
For the first time ever, it really is the lag.
At the Olympics, you'd have the fastest start in history and get disqualified.
Any reaction under a tenth of a second counts as a false start.
Flies dodge your slap because to them, your hand moves in slow motion.
Now, you catch them with chopsticks.
To react 10 times faster, your brain has to run 10 times faster.
Now you see the world like a fly does, in slow motion.
Movies run at 24 frames per second.
You'd never drop your phone again.
You'd just wait 10 times longer for it to load.
And this video for you, it lasted over 15 minutes.

styles.name: What if your X was 10 times ...? (voiced 3D simulation, second person)
styles.form: A what-if question as the first words, then a rising list of results, each a figure shown on an object, a turn that starts with 'But' two thirds in, a closing question. Measured in full in the COPY SPEC.
styles.numbers: Yastor on YouTube: 14 Shorts, median 5,950, 3 over five times the median (235x, 126x, 39x), 11 between 3,200 and 20,000 views. The same reaction film on Instagram: 231,881 likes. On TikTok (an older look): 9 posts, 195 to 1,312 views.
styles.money: The one money film in this form that was watched got 0.7x (the doubling dollar). See the COPY SPEC before choosing a subject.

styles.name: What if you ...? as one silent journey with a racing counter (Alternate Outcomes Animations)
styles.form: No voice, music only. The question sits small at the top for the first 2 to 4 s. One counter in the corner runs the whole film (DEPTH 5.00 cm to 12,742 km with SPEED x1 to x67,108,864; AIR RUNS OUT IN 2:12:57). One short caption per beat, the key word in yellow: 'The dog is concerned', 'That was the water pipe', 'You struck oil', 'The centre. You float.', 'Not China. The Indian Ocean.', 'The ocean followed you home'. The buried-alive film gives real figures ('The lid is under 1.4 m of fresh dirt', 'The dirt on the lid weighs 2.8 tonnes', 'The grave is 1.83 m deep. You are 1.78 m.') and ends on a joke ('Then a tsunami. From nowhere.'). Both hits end where they began.
styles.numbers: 41 Shorts, median 28,500, 5 over five times the median. The two hits are one unbroken journey (4 and 15 hard cuts in 46 and 45 s); the two flops jump between rooms (19 and 23 cuts) and are both money settings (a jackpot, a bank vault).
styles.money: Both money films flopped at 0.2x. Two cases, so a warning and not a rule.

styles.name: An old parable retold, then turned on the viewer (DuckModo)
styles.form: Voiced, flat 2D figures, almost no cuts (1 in 83 s). Opens on the act that looks bad, with no names: 'A starving young man reaches into a pot of rice and shoves a fistful into his mouth.' Then who saw it, the wrong judgment, the accused's own explanation, the teacher's quoted moral. At about 54 s (two thirds in) it turns to the viewer: 'That story was written down over 2,000 years ago, and we still do it every day.' Three modern cases as question and one-word verdict ('The coworker who leaves at 3:00? Lazy. Until you learn she's driving her mother to dialysis.'), a callback ('We see the hand go into the pot. We never see the soot.') and a closing question.
styles.numbers: DuckModo: 2,330 subscribers, 24 Shorts, median 12,500, 3 over five times (60x, 18x, 9x). Mohan Yagami: 6 of 21 over five times. Spiritual Stories: 6 of 24. Only the Confucius film was watched.
styles.money: Fits by nature (greed, price, patience are parable subjects), and it is the runner-up for copying: one watched film is too few for a copy spec.

styles.name: In This Town (first person, one rule, one unease)
styles.form: The rule in sentence one ('In this town, every house has a number on the door.'), what it means, two neighbours as proof, 'It is never wrong', then the crack ('Our door says four. There are three of us'), a test by the narrator, an official who leaves fast, and an open ending on the same object ('It still said four.'). 190 words in 55 s (3.45 a second), 35 cuts. The form of the craftee and VoidCast stories is in niche3d_2026-11-21.md.
styles.numbers: Titles of this kind in the listings: 62 Shorts from 9 channels, 13 over five times their channel, none over a million views. Just Benny: 19 Shorts, median 19,000, none over five times.
styles.money: Already the daily town reel. Nothing in this listing argues for more of it.

Everybody In This Town Is an NPC. Except Me.

styles.name: Would you rather, worked out in front of you
styles.form: Prince Ea, a real person behind a table of real cash: the choice in the first 6 s ('would you rather have $1 million or one penny that doubled every day for 30 days'), what most people do, 'I'm going to tell you why you should take the penny', then the days on sticky notes (day 1, 2, 3, 8, 15, 16, 21, 27, 28, 30) to '$5.4 million'. 106 words in 44 s, no closing question. Factsphere's '$1 Million' title is an explainer over a real clip (a dam spillway), not a story.
styles.numbers: '$0.01 vs 1 Million': 48.4 million views, 317 times Prince Ea's median, 1.5 million likes. Titles with 'would you' or a dilemma: 341 Shorts from 123 channels, 13% over five times.
styles.money: The same subject as Yastor's 0.7x film, told as a choice with the sum done in front of the viewer. Top comment (15,000 likes): 'My damass thought I'll have 30 cent on the last day'. A live presenter, so not a 3D style to copy as it stands.

listed.title: Criminal life or a little child life?
Can you solve these Moral Dilemmas?

styles.name: He / She drama in blocky figures (Bloopo)
styles.form: All dialogue, no narrator, 39 cuts in 52 s (one every 1.3 s), 176 words. A whole reversal in under a minute: the boss ('You're worthless ... Go to that rusty shed you live in'), the family with no milk, the find, the price ('Over 10 million dollars') at 32 s, and the mirror line at the end: 'I bought the cave. If you want to stay, I have a rusty shed you can live in.'
styles.numbers: 3.1 million subscribers, 41 Shorts all over 100,000, median 2.3 million, best 4.3 times the median: a studio with an audience, steady, no outliers.
styles.money: Many of its titles are about money (a diamond, $50M left to him, a millionaire brother, secretly rich). It is a serial studio's look and cast, which a single style spec does not carry over.

styles.name: Staged kindness and greed tales (photoreal scenes or AI pictures, no words)
styles.form: Photoreal street scenes (acted or generated: the frames do not say which) or image-model pictures of golden objects, music only, 47 s and 7 cuts in the one watched. The title carries the story: 'He / She [did X]... [But / Then / Until] [Y]'. Nothing is said, so there is nothing to transcribe.
styles.numbers: The biggest raw numbers in the slice: 1,033 Shorts with kindness, greed, patience or karma in the title, 284 over a million views, 19% over five times their channel.
styles.money: No narration and no figures: outside what a voiced money reel can copy.

listed.title: She Was Poor... But Always Chose Kindness
Be Kind Everywhere... No Matter Who You Are

styles.name: Two stick figures, two choices, one counter (StickTheory)
styles.form: No words, one shot of 20 s: two labelled figures (PERFECTIONIST, FINISHER) on black, one paints a single plank, the other finishes the fence. 'Lottery vs Saving' (stills only) has the labels HOPING and BUILDING and a day counter (DAY 54, DAY 216).
styles.numbers: 667 subscribers, median 3,800, best 31,000. Its money film ('Lottery vs Saving') got 0.3x.

styles.name: Absurd sketch with a twist or a loop
styles.form: Named comics with their own voice: Luka Big Pants (a fake 1990s game with choices that all give the same answer), It's Just Bits (a genie sketch of 34 s and 100 words that loops; top comment, 7,200 likes: 'Hollup, this loops'), Cyanide and Happiness (wordless), Low Budget Stories (a wojak montage to music, 170 s).
styles.numbers: 7.7 million, 1.8 million, 1.2 million, 1.9 million and 4.6 million views.
styles.money: A comic's hand, not a form.

styles.name: Timeline and comparison what-ifs (WatchData)
styles.form: Wordless cards to music (WatchData), or a map that redraws itself (Mapper Maniac, Aeon Report: listed only). Yastor's two country films belong to this family by subject.
styles.numbers: WatchData: median 39,000; its what-if titles 0.4x to 13.6x. Mapper Maniac: median 740,500, 6 of 48 over five times.
styles.money: A country or a person as the subject, not a price.
